what: Aurora Innovation is building self-driving software for long-haul trucks. It has begun driverless freight runs in Texas and partners with Paccar, Volvo and Continental to build the hardware.
customers: Freight carriers and shippers who would pay per mile for driverless trucking, through partners such as Werner, Schneider and Uber Freight.
money: early driverless and supervised freight runs and partner payments
moat: A decade of autonomy development with manufacturing partnerships already signed, in a field where the capital and validation requirements have eliminated most competitors.
risks: $933M of net loss and $800M of negative free cash flow against $7.0M of revenue
Only $221M of cash: it will need to raise more money
Driverless trucking has been promised for a decade and commercial scale is still ahead
opportunities: Driverless commercial runs have actually started in Texas, which most competitors have not achieved
Partnerships with Paccar and Volvo mean the trucks would be factory-built rather than retrofitted
Analysts see about 201% upside, though with enormous disagreement
watch: Driverless miles run commercially and the cash position.
